source.title_on_document: The impact of AI-supported instructional interventions on students' creative thinking: a meta-analysis of 56 experimental studies

supplement.holds: Not known; only the abstract was read.

paper_design_summary: Meta-analysis of 56 empirical studies (9,643 participants in total) of AI-supported instructional interventions aimed at students' creative thinking. It reports a pooled standardized mean difference using R 4.3.2 and examines moderators including stages of AI development and roles of AI. The abstract does not identify the included AI technologies or establish their generative-AI coverage.

eligibility.reason: Synthesis context evidence: a meta-analysis of 56 studies, with no original randomized people study described (OpenAlex W4414510278, abstract, sentence 1). The abstract does not identify the included AI technologies, assignment methods, per-study analyzed samples, or whether creativity was scored on produced outputs. The total of 9,643 participants is pooled across studies and does not establish criterion 2 for a primary experiment. Only the abstract was read; the confidence interval, number of effect sizes, and search end date are not stated.

one_line_finding: A meta-analysis of 56 studies involving 9,643 total participants reports a moderate positive effect of AI-supported instruction on students' creative thinking (SMD = 0.54; OpenAlex abstract, sentences 2-3); the included AI technologies are not identified.
